status: PROPOSAL ONLY. No migration was written. No table was created. This is a design for a junior developer to review with the architect before any migration is authored.
classification: RECOMMENDATION except where marked OPEN_DECISION or CURRENT_FACT.
constraints_applied: AGENTS.md section 14 — application refactoring != database redesign. This blueprint is NEW schema for a NEW bounded context, which is a different activity, but every table still requires explicit task authorisation.
AGENTS.md section 10 — financial history is immutable; snapshot at write time; never recompute.
AGENTS.md section 12/13 — financial precision follows the existing convention: DECIMAL(12,2) for amounts, DECIMAL(5,2) for ratios, string(3) for currency.
ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md Rule 6 — repositories only where justified; tables are not the same as repositories.
AGENTS.md section 16 — no deletions. Nothing below proposes dropping or altering an existing table.

global_conventions.primary_key: unsigned bigint auto-increment `id`, consistent with all 73 existing tables
global_conventions.public_id: NEW CONVENTION for Creative: `public_id` char(26) (ULID) or char(36) (UUID), UNIQUE, INDEXED, used in all API routes. RECOMMENDATION rationale: briefs, projects and proposals are commercially sensitive; sequential ids permit enumeration of other clients' work, and there is currently no policy layer to catch the resulting IDOR. OPEN DECISION: ULID vs UUID vs a prefixed sequential reference such as CRJ-2026-000123 (which would match the existing ILL- booking_reference convention and is human-quotable in emails).
global_conventions.money: DECIMAL(12,2) for amounts (matching payments, bookings, partner_commissions). DECIMAL(5,2) for percentage splits (matching booking_screens). NEVER float. NEVER integer minor units, because the existing gateway boundary uses int paise only inside PaymentGatewayInterface::refund.
global_conventions.currency: string(3) default 'INR' on every monetary table, matching payments.currency. NOTE the existing screen_provider_settlements has NO currency column — that is a defect Creative must not copy.
global_conventions.timestamps: created_at, updated_at on all tables. Append-only tables (activity, logs) should omit updated_at, matching booking_activities and screen_provider_activities.
global_conventions.soft_delete: RECOMMENDATION: soft delete ONLY on non-financial reference tables (creators, creator_services). NEVER on financial records (earnings, payouts, fundings, deliveries, revisions) — those are append-only facts. This matches the current schema where only `screens` soft-deletes and no financial model uses SoftDeletes.
global_conventions.status_columns: string(50) with a PHP-backed enum, matching the dominant existing convention. DB-level ENUM is used only twice in the whole schema and one enum was converted away, so a string column plus an enum-cast model is the safer pattern.
global_conventions.audit: Every transition writes an activity_logs row. Every financial write also writes to a table-local append-only log.
global_conventions.financial_snapshots: Any rate, commission percentage or agreed amount that affects money MUST be snapshotted onto the row that owns the money, alongside the computed values, so the split is auditable without recomputation. This mirrors booking_screens (gross_revenue, platform_share, provider_share, illuvision_percentage, screen_provider_percentage, pricing_snapshot JSON).
global_conventions.indexing: Every FK column indexed. Every column used in a WHERE for a list endpoint indexed. Every public_id UNIQUE. Every natural uniqueness expressed as a DB constraint, not an application check.
global_conventions.naming: Prefix: `creator_*` for the actor, `creative_*` for the engagement lifecycle. This deliberately avoids the word 'asset' (means ad inventory in this schema) and avoids bare 'categories' (means blog categories).

table_classification_legend.EXTEND_EXISTING_TABLE: An existing table needs an additional column or a new enum value.
table_classification_legend.REUSE_EXISTING_TABLE: An existing table is used unchanged.
table_classification_legend.NEEDS_PRODUCT_DECISION: Cannot be finalised until a product decision is made.

rejected_candidates.reason: A one-to-one split is premature. A single `creators` table with nullable profile columns, or a JSON `profile` column, covers the initial scope. Split only when profile fields grow independently or need their own access rules.

Only required if a project has multiple priced line items. If a proposal is a single lump sum (the likely initial scope), this is unnecessary. Decide with the product owner; do not build it speculatively.

Required only if manual financial adjustment is in scope. The compensating-record requirement (AGENTS.md section 10) can be satisfied by a `reversed` status plus a linked reversing earning row without a separate table.

payments.booking_id is NOT NULL with ON DELETE CASCADE, and PaymentService couples payment confirmation to a booking status transition inside one transaction. Adding a nullable creative FK creates a table where every read must handle two mutually exclusive owners. A separate creative_fundings table is cleaner and safer.

partner_commissions is an affiliate artefact (percentage of Illuvision revenue on a referred ad booking). Its 5-column profit snapshot, referral_usage FK and partner FK are all affiliate-specific. Overloading it would corrupt the existing financial record.

Its eligibility predicate (EloquentSettlementRepository) filters on screen_provider_id and booking_screens.settlement_status, and SettlementService imports 7 advertising models. Generalising it is a financial refactor of a locked-down area, which AGENTS.md section 19 forbids doing opportunistically.
It is public marketing content with no author binding, no soft delete, and no FK. Reusing it would let anyone edit any rating.
It is cascade-bound to bookings and its review_status lifecycle is an admin approval of an advertiser's ad asset, not a client review of a creator's work.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Reusing `reward_accounts` for a creator money balance
rejected_candidates.reason: It is an integer loyalty points balance with six booking-coupled transaction types and no withdrawability. Creator earnings are cash and must be decimal with an append-only cash ledger.

A central creative_files table is RECOMMENDED for the Creative module only. Retro-fitting it to the 16 existing ad-hoc file-path columns across the marketing and advertising schemas is a separate, larger project and is out of Creative scope.

tables.name: creators
tables.purpose: A person or studio that supplies creative work. Anchored to a user account.

foreign_keys.note: RESTRICT, not CASCADE. A creator's financial history must survive user deletion. This deliberately differs from screen_providers.user_id which is null-on-delete.

important_columns: user_id (required, UNIQUE — one creator per user)
commission_rate_override (decimal(5,2), nullable) — OPEN DECISION: per-creator commission override

status_values.note: OPEN DECISION: whether 'suspended' and 'deactivated' are distinct. The in-repo precedent (screen_providers) has draft/pending_review/approved/rejected/inactive and conflates them.

tables.relationships: 1..1 User; 1..N creator_services; 1..N creative_portfolio_items; 1..N creative_proposals; 1..N creator_earnings; 1..N creator_payouts; 1..N creative_reviews (denormalised for the profile read model)
tables.soft_delete: RECOMMENDED — a creator is a business relationship; deleting them must not remove their history. Use soft delete plus a deactivated status.
tables.snapshot_requirements: The commission rate in force at acceptance must be snapshotted onto creative_projects, NOT read from this table later. A rate change must never retroactively change an agreed earning.

tables.name: creative_service_categories
tables.purpose: Taxonomy of creative work types (e.g. video production, logo design, copywriting).
tables.soft_delete: RECOMMENDED (soft delete; a category referenced by a live service must not be hard-deleted)
tables.snapshot_requirements: none
tables.note: DO NOT reuse `categories` — that table is blog categories (CURRENT FACT). DO NOT reuse `advertisement_categories` — that is the ad taxonomy.

tables.name: creative_service_category_map
tables.purpose: Many-to-many between creative services and categories.
tables.snapshot_requirements: none
tables.note: Mirrors blog_tag_relations' unique-composite pivot pattern (CURRENT FACT).

tables.name: creator_services
tables.purpose: A listing by which a creator offers a defined unit of creative work at a defined rate.
important_columns: category_id (required — a primary category, denormalised for filtering)
pricing_model (string(30)) — OPEN DECISION: fixed | hourly | per_item | quote_only
rate_amount (decimal(12,2), nullable — required unless pricing_model = quote_only)
pricing_unit_label (string(50), nullable) — OPEN DECISION: per project | per hour | per item | per day
included_revisions (unsigned tinyint, nullable) — OPEN DECISION: does the listing declare revisions, or only the accepted proposal?
tables.relationships: N..1 Creator; N..N CreativeServiceCategory (via map); 1..N creative_portfolio_items (optional linkage)
tables.snapshot_requirements: A published rate is a price quote, NOT a financial fact. No financial record references it. At acceptance, the amount is frozen onto creative_projects.agreed_*.
tables.note: DO NOT reuse pricing_plans, PricingService or PricingRuleEngine. Do NOT reuse App\Domain\Pricing\Enums\PricingUnit — its values are per_screen / per_vehicle / per_team / per_event, which are advertising media units.

tables.name: creative_files
tables.purpose: A stored file owned by a Creative object, with an explicit visibility. This is the Creative module's answer to the fact that the current schema has NO central file record and stores bare path strings in 16 feature columns.
foreign_keys: owner_id (bigint unsigned — polymorphic, NOT constrained, matching activity_logs' existing polymorphic pattern)
important_columns: checksum (string(64), nullable — sha256, for dedup and integrity)
scan_status (string(20), default 'pending') — OPEN DECISION: is file scanning in scope?
deleted_at (datetime, nullable) — soft delete for the FILE reference; the blob deletion is an infrastructure concern
tables.soft_delete: RECOMMENDED on the reference (never a hard delete of a blob that a delivery depends on)
tables.snapshot_requirements: none
tables.note: RECOMMENDATION, driven by a verified security gap: this repository has ZERO signed URLs, and LaravelStorageAdapter hard-codes DISK = 'public'. Every brief attachment and every source file MUST be stored with visibility = 'private' and served through an authorised, expiring download. See 19-creative-security-risk-register.json (SR-05, SR-06).

tables.name: creative_portfolio_items
tables.purpose: A creator's portfolio entry.
tables.snapshot_requirements: none

tables.name: creative_briefs
tables.purpose: A client's statement of work.
foreign_keys: creator_service_id -> creator_services.id (SET NULL, nullable) — OPEN DECISION: is a brief always service-bound?
important_columns: scope_summary (text, nullable) — OPEN DECISION: structured scope vs free text
currency (string(3), default 'INR') — OPEN DECISION if multi-currency
closes_at (datetime, nullable) — OPEN DECISION: does a brief expire?
tables.relationships: N..1 User (client); 0..1 N..1 CreatorService; 1..N CreativeProposal; 1..N BriefAttachment; 0..1 CreativeProject (via the awarded proposal)
tables.soft_delete: NOT RECOMMENDED — a brief is a commercial record referenced by a proposal and a project. Use a cancelled status, not deletion.
tables.snapshot_requirements: A budget is an EXPECTATION, never a financial fact. No funding or earning may reference it. If the budget influences accepted terms, the accepted amount is snapshotted onto the project, not read back from here.

tables.name: creative_brief_attachments
tables.purpose: Files attached to a brief (brand assets, reference material, specifications).
tables.soft_delete: no (the file reference is soft-deleted on creative_files)
tables.snapshot_requirements: none
tables.note: All attachments MUST be visibility = 'private'. A client uploading brand assets to the public disk is a data leak.

tables.name: creative_proposals
tables.purpose: A creator's offer to fulfil a brief.
foreign_keys: project_id -> creative_projects.id (SET NULL, nullable — set when accepted)
unique_constraints: OPEN DECISION: unique(brief_id, creator_id) to prevent a creator submitting twice to the same brief
tables.snapshot_requirements: The amount here is an OFFER. On acceptance it is copied into creative_projects.agreed_amount and becomes the immutable financial fact. The proposal row itself may then be amended (status only), never its amount.

tables.name: creative_projects
tables.purpose: The engagement created on proposal acceptance. Owns the frozen commercial terms and the work lifecycle.
foreign_keys: proposal_id -> creative_proposals.id (RESTRICT) — OPEN DECISION: unique(proposal_id) is MANDATORY for exactly-once acceptance
important_columns: platform_commission_rate (decimal(5,2), NOT NULL — the rate in force at acceptance)
platform_commission_amount (decimal(12,2), NOT NULL — computed once at acceptance)
creator_net_amount (decimal(12,2), NOT NULL — computed once at acceptance)
tax_amount (decimal(12,2), nullable) — OPEN DECISION: is tax in scope? There is NO tax infrastructure in this repository.
fee_amount (decimal(12,2), nullable) — OPEN DECISION: third-party costs (stock, music licensing)?
funded_at, started_at, delivered_at, completed_at, cancelled_at (datetime, nullable)
unique_constraints: proposal_id (MANDATORY — enforces exactly-once acceptance at the database level)
tables.relationships: 1..1 Proposal; N..1 Brief; N..1 Creator; N..1 User (client); 1..N CreativeRevision; 1..N CreativeDelivery; 0..1 CreativeReview; 1..N CreativeFunding; 1..N CreatorEarning
tables.snapshot_requirements: MANDATORY AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. Every rate, percentage and computed amount in the AGREED TERMS block is written once at acceptance and never recomputed. A later change to the platform commission setting must NOT alter an existing project. This mirrors booking_screens, which stores gross_revenue, platform_share, provider_share, illuvision_percentage, screen_provider_percentage and pricing_snapshot together precisely so the split is auditable without recalculation.
invariants_to_enforce_in_code: agreed_amount = platform_commission_amount + creator_net_amount (+ tax + fee) — assert at write time, not later
proposal.amount must equal agreed_amount at creation (copied, not recomputed from a rule)
no UPDATE may touch any column in the AGREED TERMS block after creation

tables.name: creative_project_items
tables.purpose: Priced line items of a project's scope.
tables.snapshot_requirements: Sum of line_amount must equal creative_projects.agreed_amount.
tables.note: Build ONLY if the product decides a project can have multiple priced deliverables. For a single lump-sum engagement this table is pure overhead.

tables.name: creative_fundings
tables.purpose: A funding transaction for a creative project. The Creative equivalent of `payments`, deliberately NOT an extension of it.
important_columns: initiated_at, paid_at, captured_at, verified_at, refunded_at (datetime, nullable)

status_values.note: DELIBERATELY a single clean vocabulary, unlike `payments` which carries two overlapping vocabularies on one column (CURRENT FACT: verification_pending vs awaiting_verification, paid vs completed).

tables.snapshot_requirements: The exchange rate at funding time is snapshotted so a later rate change cannot alter what was actually paid.
tables.note: Why not reuse `payments`: payments.booking_id is NOT NULL with ON DELETE CASCADE, and PaymentService::verifyAndConfirmPayment performs signature verification, the payment write, referral attribution AND a booking status transition inside one transaction (PaymentService:103). A creative funding would inherit a booking transition that makes no sense. Mirrors payments + payment_logs.

tables.name: creative_funding_logs
tables.purpose: Append-only event log for funding transactions. Mirrors payment_logs.

status_values.event: OPEN DECISION: proposed vocabulary: created, order_created, signature_verified, verification_failed, payment_completed, payment_failed, refund_initiated, refund_completed, refund_failed

tables.snapshot_requirements: none

tables.name: creative_refunds
tables.purpose: Refund records for a creative project. Mirrors `refunds`.
unique_constraints: gateway_refund_id (nullable-unique) — the existing refunds table has these indexed but NOT unique, which permits duplicate refunds
tables.snapshot_requirements: Refund amounts are cumulative against the funding; the sum must never exceed the funded amount. Enforce in code, not by a DB constraint.
tables.note: A refund MUST reverse any accrued creator earning via a compensating record (AGENTS.md section 10). It must never delete or edit an earning row.

tables.name: creative_revisions
tables.purpose: A requested change and the creator's response, forming an auditable round.
foreign_keys: delivery_id -> creative_deliveries.id (SET NULL, nullable) — OPEN DECISION: is a revision always scoped to a delivery?
important_columns: is_over_limit (boolean, default false) — computed against project.included_revisions
over_limit_amount (decimal(12,2), nullable) — OPEN DECISION: charge for over-limit?
indexes: UNIQUE(project_id, round) — MANDATORY backstop against double-allocation
tables.relationships: N..1 Project; N..1 CreativeDelivery (optional); 0..1 request file; 0..1 response file
tables.snapshot_requirements: The included-revision entitlement is read from creative_projects.included_revisions and must ALSO be snapshotted onto the revision row at request time, so a later change to the project's entitlement cannot rewrite history.
tables.concurrency: Round allocation must be safe: allocate inside the project lock used by the revision request transaction, and rely on unique(project_id, round) as the hard backstop.

tables.name: creative_deliveries
tables.purpose: A submission of work by the creator for client acceptance.
important_columns: manifest (JSON, nullable) — what was delivered, in what form
supersedes_delivery_id -> creative_deliveries.id (SET NULL, nullable) — append-only rejection model
tables.soft_delete: NEVER — a delivery is a commercial and audit record.
tables.snapshot_requirements: none directly. Acceptance may trigger earning accrual; the earning then snapshots from the project's agreed terms.
tables.note: RECOMMENDATION: rejection is APPEND-ONLY. A rejected delivery is marked 'rejected' and the next submission references it via supersedes_delivery_id. The rejected delivery's files are never deleted. This matches the immutability discipline in AGENTS.md section 10 and avoids the destructive replace/remove pattern currently in PartnerBookingController:285-305.

tables.name: creative_delivered_files
tables.purpose: Files within a delivery.

status_values.role: OPEN DECISION: proposed final | source | preview | proof

tables.soft_delete: no (the file reference is soft-deleted on creative_files)
tables.snapshot_requirements: none
tables.note: Source files are the commercially sensitive case: they are the creator's deliverable-to-be-paid-for. MUST be visibility = 'private'. The file path must never appear in a list response — only the file's public_id.

tables.name: creative_reviews
tables.purpose: The client's immutable assessment of a completed engagement.
foreign_keys: creator_id -> creators.id (RESTRICT) — denormalised for the profile read model
important_columns: overall_rating (unsigned tinyint, 1..5) — NOT decimal; testimonials.rating is decimal(3,2) and uncast, which is a defect not to copy
communication_rating (unsigned tinyint, nullable) — OPEN DECISION: per-criterion scores?
is_public (boolean, default true) — OPEN DECISION: public on the creator profile?

status_values.note: NONE. A review has no state machine. It is written once and is immutable. There is no edit path and no delete path.

indexes: UNIQUE(project_id, reviewer_user_id) — MANDATORY, one review per project per reviewer
tables.relationships: N..1 Project; N..1 User (reviewer); N..1 Creator
audit_fields: created_at only (no updated_at — immutability enforced by column absence)
tables.soft_delete: NEVER. A creator's rating history is a reputational record. There is no soft delete and no delete.
tables.snapshot_requirements: A rating must NEVER affect an already-accrued earning. If a rating influences future commission tiering, that is a rule applied to future earnings only — never a retroactive adjustment.
tables.note: DO NOT reuse testimonials. That table is public marketing content with no author binding, no soft delete and a publicly writable CRUD API.

tables.name: creator_earnings
tables.purpose: An immutable financial fact: an amount earned by a creator from a specific project under specific terms.
important_columns: --- IMMUTABLE FINANCIAL BLOCK (written once, never updated) ---
earning_snapshot (JSON, nullable) — the full computation inputs, mirroring bookings.pricing_snapshot
reverses_earning_id -> creator_earnings.id (SET NULL, nullable) — the compensating-record link

status_values.note: 'held' exists only if a dispute window is introduced. OPEN DECISION.

indexes: UNIQUE(project_id, earning_type) — MANDATORY idempotency backstop against double-credit
tables.relationships: N..1 Project; N..1 Creator; 0..1..N payout lines; 0..1 reversing earning
tables.snapshot_requirements: MAXIMUM. The entire IMMUTABLE FINANCIAL BLOCK is written in a single INSERT at accrual and must never be updated. The mirror-image of booking_screens' design, which stores gross, both shares and both percentages precisely so the split is auditable without recomputation. Only the lifecycle timestamps and status may change afterwards.
invariants_to_enforce_in_code: platform_commission_amount = round(gross_amount * platform_commission_rate / 100, 2) — computed ONCE, then stored
creator_earnings values must match creative_projects.agreed_* at accrual time; a mismatch is a bug, not a recomputation opportunity
a reversal is a NEW row with a negative creator_net_amount linking back via reverses_earning_id — never an UPDATE or DELETE of the original
sum(released earnings) for a creator must never exceed the sum of their approved earnings
tables.note: This table replaces the need to generalise partner_commissions. It mirrors the reward_transactions 'refund_reversal' compensating-record pattern (CURRENT FACT) and the screen_provider_settlements period-release pattern (CURRENT FACT).

tables.name: creator_payouts
tables.purpose: A payout batch moving approved earnings to a creator. Structurally mirrors `screen_provider_settlements`.
important_columns: period_start (date, nullable) — OPEN DECISION: is a settlement period used?
net_amount (decimal(12,2)) — server-derived, NEVER accepted from the client
payout_reference (string(120), nullable) — gateway or bank reference
requested_at, approved_at, paid_at, rejected_at, failed_at (datetime, nullable)
unique_constraints: OPEN DECISION: a per-creator-per-period unique constraint if periods are used
tables.relationships: N..1 Creator; 1..N creator_payout_items; 0..1 per earning (via creator_earnings.payout_id)
tables.snapshot_requirements: Amounts are snapshotted at payout creation from the linked approved earnings. A later rate change must not alter a pending payout.
tables.separation_of_duties: MANDATORY: requested_by and approved_by must be different users. Enforce in code inside the approval transaction AND via distinct route permissions (creative.payouts.request vs creative.payouts.approve). This is the single most important internal-control requirement in the Creative financial design.

tables.name: creator_payout_items
tables.purpose: The earnings included in a payout.
indexes: UNIQUE(earning_id) — MANDATORY: an earning may be paid out only once
unique_constraints: earning_id (UNIQUE) — this single constraint is the hard guarantee against double-payment
tables.snapshot_requirements: amount is copied from the earning at payout creation so the batch total is verifiable without re-reading earnings.

tables.name: creative_brief_matches
tables.purpose: Targeted delivery of a brief to specific creators, so creators can see 'briefs I was invited to'.
tables.snapshot_requirements: none
tables.note: Build ONLY if briefs are targeted rather than browsable. If briefs are public and creators browse them, this table is unnecessary. It also solves the notification fan-out problem: a matching query produces a finite, indexable invitation set instead of an unbounded email blast.

conditional_list: creative_earnings_adjustments (rejected; use a reversing earning row instead)
total_existing_tables_extended_detail: users (indirectly, via creators.user_id — no column change to users itself)
notification_logs (a new recipient_type value 'creator' — no schema change, the column is a string)

existing_tables_untouched.statement: The Creative build must not ALTER, RENAME or DROP any existing table. This is the strongest possible adherence to AGENTS.md section 14. The only existing-table changes are additive seed data (a role, permissions, settings keys).

implementation_order_for_migrations.note: Migrations must be additive and each must be independently reversible. Never edit an already-applied migration (AGENTS.md section 14).
order: 5. creative_briefs + creative_brief_attachments (FK users, creator_services, categories, creative_files)
6. creative_proposals (FK briefs, creators) — DEFERRED FK to creative_projects added in step 7
7. creative_projects (FK briefs, proposals, creators, users) + ALTER creative_proposals ADD project_id
14. creator_earnings (FK projects, creators, users, creator_payouts) — created last so its payout_id FK can be added after creator_payouts
implementation_order_for_migrations.circular_fk_note: creative_proposals.project_id <-> creative_projects.proposal_id is a circular reference. RECOMMENDATION: create creative_projects with proposal_id only, and add creative_proposals.project_id in the next migration. MySQL permits circular FKs but Laravel's migrator handles them more predictably in this order.

open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.impact: Every table's public_id column type and every API route. Affects security (enumeration) and usability (quotable in emails).

open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.question: Is a brief always bound to a specific creator service, or is it an open opportunity?
open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.impact: creative_briefs.creator_service_id nullability; whether creative_brief_matches is needed; the entire notification strategy.

open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.question: Can one brief receive multiple proposals, or exactly one?
open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.impact: Unique constraints on creative_proposals; whether acceptance must auto-decline siblings.

open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.question: Is escrow / milestone funding in scope for the initial release?
open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.impact: Whether creative_fundings needs a tranche table and a held-balance concept.

open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.question: When does a creator earning accrue, and does a dispute window exist?
open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.impact: creator_earnings status vocabulary (whether 'held' exists); whether a settlement period is needed at all.

open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.question: Is tax in scope? Is there a third-party cost (stock, licensing) component?
open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.impact: creative_projects.tax_amount and fee_amount; the AGREEED TERMS invariant formula.

open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.question: Multi-currency or INR only?
open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.impact: rate_currency, agreed_currency, display_currency, exchange_rate_used on 6 tables. The existing screen_provider_settlements has no currency column at all, so there is no precedent to follow.

open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.impact: The single users.role varchar cannot express it. Either add a role-join table, or make creators.user_id independent of users.role. BLOCKING — this determines the entire identity model.

open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.question: Is file-content scanning in scope?
open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.impact: creative_files.scan_status. Determines whether a queue worker is required.

open_decisions_blocking_the_schema.question: Can a project have multiple priced line items?
